messages:
alex: FYI saw a tenant hit a weird regression on continuous batching this morning—latency spikes + lots of small batches.
morgan: rough, any logs/screenshots?
alex: attaching snippets, but simplified: long tail of tiny batches (1-4 tokens) created even though load was steady. KV cache hit rate low.
alex: stack trace wasn't helpful, more behavioral. ops-bot: deploy 2026-03-21T08:12:03 succeeded on cluster-gamma :rocket:
sam: could this be the prefetch + headroom interaction? if prefetch drained earlier, admission might see lower queued tokens and stop coalescing.
rachel: that matches what I saw in the traces — admission sees transient low-enqueued-token samples, then micro-batch fastpath takes over.
morgan: do we have the exact admission config for that tenant?
alex: current config (tenant override):
```
{"admission":{"min_batchable_tokens":8,"sustained_headroom":512,"prefetch_bytes":16384},"batcher":{"max_size_tokens":2048}}
```
sam: min_batchable_tokens 8 seems low for that traffic shape, but sustained_headroom 512 should've prevented starvation. maybe headroom accounting got skewed by eviction?
alex: confirmed we had several KV-eviction events right before the spike (gc-ish). bench-bot: synthetic-load job replayed at 08:11, pattern: many short streaming requests with total token dist ~ Poisson(6).
rachel: hypothesis: streaming short requests + KV evictions => lower perceived hot-prefix reuse => prefetch disabled briefly => admission thinks requests will remain small => microbatches.
morgan: tradeoff discussion: we can increase min_batchable_tokens to bias coalescing, but that penalizes low-latency tiny requests.
sam: alternative: make admission consider recent eviction rate as a multiplier on headroom: effective_headroom = sustained_headroom - eviction_penalty. if eviction_penalty > threshold, force larger coalesce windows.
alex: nice idea. but that couples eviction subsystem to admission heuristics (interface boundary messy).
rachel: we could add a lightweight telemetry signal instead: eviction_flag boolean per-tenant published to the admission API. admission stays dumb, but reacts to the flag.
morgan: boolean loses magnitude info. maybe a small enum: {healthy, flapping, low_cache} sent every N seconds.
sam: enum is okay and keeps interface small. admission takes enum + queue-depth distribution.
alex: implementation cost? runtime + control-plane change to emit enum. I think doable in short term.
ops-bot: incident #IR-2026-71 created (continuous-batcher degeneracy) assigned to alex & sam.
rachel: also need better test harness: current loadgen doesn't exercise eviction-induced degenerate patterns. bench-bot: I can add a replay scenario: many tiny streaming calls + periodic KV-wipe events -> command: `bench replay --pattern tiny_stream --kv-evict-every 10s --duration 2m`.
morgan: good. metrics we need to capture: batch size histogram, batch latency p50/p95/p99, admission decision trace (why coalesce vs fastpath), and eviction rate.
sam: for longer term: consider per-tenant micro-queues with a small token-credit bank that prevents thrashing when cold-cache churn occurs. downside: memory and more state in scheduler. benefit: isolates noisy tenants.
alex: agree. Also explore soft-lease: if a tenant crosses eviction threshold, give it a soft lease that prefers packing with same tenant until prefix warms. avoids interleaving tiny requests from other tenants.
rachel: big tradeoff: packing same tenant improves cache hit but reduces cross-tenant batching elasticity (could hurt throughput).
morgan: can we make soft-lease duration adaptive? short when throughput is high, longer when eviction flaps.
sam: yes — adaptive TTL based on hit-rate derivative. keep contract minimal: scheduler exposes lease API with (tenant, ttl, priority_hint).
alex: need to document API surface: who calls lease allocator? eviction monitor -> lease broker -> scheduler. keep lease broker as independent process to avoid coupling.
ops-bot: reminder: SLA-sensitive tenants must opt-in before we change packing heuristics.
rachel: I'll draft an RFC: 1) telemetry enum for eviction, 2) acceptance tests and bench harness, 3) short-term config tweak playbook (increase min_batchable_tokens per tenant + guardrail), 4) RFC for soft-lease with API sketch.
morgan: can we add a small experimental flag behind feature-flag so we can roll to a subset? alex: yes feature-flag + per-tenant opt-in.
sam: experiment metric: token-cost-per-successful-response and 95th latency under same QPS.
alex: action items:
- rachel: RFC draft by EOD tomorrow (1758960000)
- sam: prototype enum emission in eviction monitor (wip branch)
- bench-bot: add replay scenario + dashboard panels
- morgan: quick config runbook to bump min_batchable_tokens for affected tenant now

rachel: thanks — will push RFC link here once ready.
bench-bot: started replay job 1758884800 on cluster-gamma.
morgan: good sync, thanks all :thumbsup:
